concerns.text: Tasks T121–T126 introduce a new scope of 'Physical Validity & Measurement Standards' documentation and approximation traceability that is not authorized by spec.md (which defines success only via FR-001–FR-008 and SC-001–SC-003). This violates the constraint preservation principle by adding unrequested deliverables to satisfy simulated reviewer personas rather than project requirements.

Task T020b-calc specifies using 'psi4 --input ... optimize energy', which attempts geometry optimization. This contradicts spec.md FR-004 and plan.md Principle VI, which mandate that DFT calculations MUST use the exact same optimized geometries generated by DFTB+ in FR-002. This is a semantic weakening of the protocol consistency constraint.

Task T022 defines the output reports/evaluation.json to include 'error_bars' (standard deviations) and 't_test' statistics. While the t-test is required, the spec.md SC-002 only requires measuring MAE and performing a paired t-test to evaluate the difference; the inclusion of 'error_bars' is an unrequested artifact that may lead to implementation waste if the spec does not define how these are to be used or verified.

Task T121 requires citing 'simulated' reviewer personas (e.g., Rosalind Franklin, Richard Feynman) in project reports. This violates constitution.md Principle II (Verified Accuracy), which requires all external citations to be verified against primary sources. Simulated AI personas are not verifiable primary sources, making this task constitutionally invalid.

Task T010 (Validate Data Schema) depends on data/raw/barrier_dataset.csv, but the preceding tasks T004c-extract and T004c-normalize are marked as incomplete. Without a defined fallback or explicit error handling for the missing input file in T010 itself, the pipeline will fail silently or crash without satisfying the 'log verification status' requirement of FR-001 before processing.

Task T030b-sweep outputs reports/sensitivity_matrix.csv with a 'stable_flag' boolean. spec.md SC-003 only requires measuring the rank correlation; the 'stable_flag' is a derived interpretation not explicitly requested in the success criteria, potentially leading to a mismatch if the verification step expects only the raw correlation values.
